title: An ftp:// transfer configured with CURLUSESSL_NONE can reuse a pooled FTP control connection that a previous easy handle upgraded with STARTTLS and… (CVE-2026-86411)
description: This vulnerability involves an ftp:// transfer configured with CURLUSESSL_NONE reusing a pooled FTP control connection previously upgraded with STARTTLS and authenticated with a client certificate. The second FTP handle does not perform a new TLS handshake or FTP login, causing the server to continue authorizing it under the first handle's certificate identity.
aiSummary: CVE-2026-86411 describes a flaw where an ftp:// transfer using CURLUSESSL_NONE can reuse an existing pooled FTP control connection that was upgraded with STARTTLS and authenticated via a client certificate by a prior easy handle. Because the second handle skips a new TLS handshake and FTP login, the server mistakenly authorizes it under the first handle's client certificate identity, potentially allowing unauthorized access or actions under that identity.
aiImpact: The vulnerability may allow an FTP client to reuse an authenticated and encrypted control connection without re-authenticating, potentially leading to unauthorized actions performed under the identity of the first authenticated session. This could result in unintended access or privilege escalation on the FTP server if multiple FTP handles are used in the same client environment.
